name: JR5 manual gearbox removal and refitting
summary: Remove and refit the K4M manual gearbox using the K4M-applicable Renault procedure. The applicable procedure is explicitly grouped for K4J/K4M/K9K; nearby F4R/F9Q-specific values are excluded.
safety: Use an approved vehicle lift and support the engine and gearbox before removing their mounts.
Keep the steering wheel centered and immobilized before separating the steering column from the rack; the source warns of rotary-contact damage.
Disconnect the battery negative terminal first. Support the gearbox on a suitable transmission jack; do not let it hang from the clutch hydraulics or wiring.
After refitting, bleed the clutch hydraulic circuit and verify gearbox oil level.
tools: Engine support beam Mot. 1453 or equivalent approved support

removal.text: Raise the vehicle, remove the battery cover, disconnect the negative battery terminal, remove the under-engine shield and drain the gearbox oil.
Remove the front wheels, engine covers, battery, battery tray, injection ECU and its support, airflow meter and intake duct; release the gearbox control cables and wiring retainers.
Remove both front driveshafts by separating their hubs and suspension joints; on the right, release the intermediate-bearing bracket. Secure the radiator assembly before removing its crossmember.

Remove the catalyst support, starter and torque link. Disconnect the reverse-switch connector and engine speed/position sensor wiring, then disconnect the clutch hydraulic receiver without contaminating its line.
Support the engine and gearbox, remove the gearbox mount and casing fasteners, then lower the gearbox clear of the engine.
removal.warning: Do not allow the gearbox to load or damage the clutch hydraulic receiver, wiring or steering rotary contact.

installation.text: Confirm the engine-to-gearbox locating sleeves are present and correctly seated; inspect mating faces and clutch components before raising the gearbox into place.

Refit the gearbox and disturbed assemblies in reverse order, observing the sourced torque values. Do not grease the gearbox output shaft or clutch splines, as the manual warns this can damage the receiver.
Refit the driveshafts and renew the differential output seals that were removed. Refill the gearbox and set its level at the filler orifice; no capacity value is asserted here.
Reconnect and bleed the clutch hydraulic circuit, restore the brake-fluid level, reconnect the battery and perform any required vehicle learning procedures.
Check for oil and hydraulic leaks, confirm every gear selects correctly and road-test only after all supports, wheels and steering connections are secured.

checks: Gearbox oil level reaches the filler-orifice level.
Clutch hydraulic circuit is bled and has no leaks.
All forward gears and reverse engage with the engine both off and running.
No oil leaks at either differential seal or gearbox plugs.

faults.symptom: Gearbox will not separate or seat flush to the engine
faults.causes: A locating sleeve may be displaced, the clutch disc may not be centered, or the gearbox input splines may not be aligned; do not draw the assembly together with bolts.
A disturbed lip seal may be damaged, incorrectly seated or not renewed; inspect the filler and drain plugs and verify level.

safety: Support the engine and gearbox before removal.
Lock the crankshaft with the specified flywheel-locking tool; keep hands clear of pinch points.
Inspect the flywheel and crankshaft flange for damage before refitting.

installation.text: Clean the crankshaft fastener threads and degrease the flywheel-to-crankshaft seating face; inspect the flywheel condition.

removal.text: Raise and support the vehicle, disconnect the battery negative terminal, remove the under-engine shield and drain the gearbox.
Remove the wheel and release the hub nut, steering tie-rod end, anti-roll-bar link and lower joint as required to withdraw the driveshaft.

removal.text: Raise and support the vehicle, remove the left front wheel and hub nut, then disconnect the wheel-speed sensor connector.
Release the steering tie-rod end, anti-roll-bar link and lower joint; pivot the knuckle to withdraw the shaft from the hub.
Drain the gearbox, then withdraw the left shaft from the differential while protecting the output seal and CV joints.

installation.text: Inspect the lip-seal running surface and renew the differential output seal. With its protective sleeve in place, grease the gearbox-side splines with MOLYKOTE BR2.
Engage the shaft into the differential and hub without force, then refit the suspension joints and wheel hardware to the sourced torques.
Refill the gearbox and set the level at the filler orifice; reconnect the wheel-speed sensor and verify the shaft is fully seated.

removal.text: Raise and support the vehicle, remove the right front wheel and hub nut, and disconnect the wheel-speed sensor connector.
Release the steering tie-rod end, anti-roll-bar link and lower joint; pivot the knuckle to withdraw the shaft from the hub.
Drain the gearbox, remove the two intermediate-bearing bracket bolts and withdraw the shaft from the gearbox.
If the intermediate bearing requires replacement, remove the complete shaft and press the bearing off without scoring the shaft seal-running surface.

installation.text: Inspect the intermediate-bearing seat and differential seal surface. If renewing the bearing, lubricate its shaft seat and press on the new bearing by loading its inner race.
Clean and grease the bearing carrier bore; renew a damaged O-ring and the differential output seal. Grease the protected gearbox-side splines with MOLYKOTE BR2.
Engage the shaft into the differential and hub, refit the bearing bracket and suspension, and tighten disturbed hardware to its sourced values.
Refill the gearbox and set its level at the filler orifice; reconnect the wheel-speed sensor and verify correct shaft seating.

checks: The intermediate bearing is fully seated and runs smoothly.
The shaft is fully engaged and no seal leakage is present.
Wheel-speed sensor wiring is connected and routed safely.

faults.symptom: Vibration or rumble from the right front driveline
faults.causes: Inspect the intermediate bearing, its carrier fit and the CV joints.

removal.text: Disconnect the battery negative terminal, remove the battery, tray and injection ECU as required, then release the two cables from the gearbox levers and sheath stops.
Remove the gear knob and boot, console trim and console fasteners; expose and release the external control housing.
To replace an individual cable, remove the complete control assembly, open the housing, disconnect the cable ball joint, release its sheath clip and withdraw the cable.

installation.text: If the housing was opened, fit a new flat gasket. Install the replacement cable and restore the housing and heat shield.
Place the cabin gear control and gearbox levers in neutral, seat the cable sheaths in their stops and attach each cable to its corresponding ball joint. The JR5 cable system is not adjusted.
Tighten the external control housing fasteners to the sourced torque, reconnect the battery and test every gear before starting.
Refit the battery cover and tighten its fasteners to the sourced value.

checks: All gears and reverse engage smoothly with the engine off.
Cable sheath stops and retaining clips are fully seated.
No cable binds through the full shift pattern.

faults.symptom: One or more gears are difficult to select

Do not pull on the wiring; release the connector lock before separation.

removal.text: For gearbox removal, disconnect the reverse-switch connector before lowering the gearbox; release its lock and protect the wiring.
The fetched applicable manual does not document standalone switch access or removal. Use exact JR5 identification and a matching repair procedure before attempting switch replacement.

installation.text: Reconnect and secure the connector during gearbox refitting. Do not apply a torque value; none is provided in the applicable source.
With the ignition on, select reverse and confirm that both reversing lamps illuminate; return the selector to neutral and confirm the lamps extinguish.

checks: Connector lock is engaged and wiring is not strained.
Reverse lamps switch on only when reverse is engaged and ignition is on.

faults.symptom: Reverse lamps do not illuminate in reverse
faults.causes: Inspect the fuse, lamps, connector, wiring and reverse-light switch; the fetched sources do not provide a JR5-specific diagnostic sequence.
